ILLUSTRATIVE C# / BLAZOR HANDLER
// Before: notification races persistence
_ = SaveOrderAsync(order);
ShowSuccess("Order saved");

// After: confirm persistence first
await SaveOrderAsync(order);
ShowSuccess("Order saved");

02 / INCIDENT DESK

From symptom to supported conclusion.

CASE FILE / QL-001
RACE CONDITIONDEMONSTRATION CASE

Success reported before
the save completes.

A fictional order workflow showing how I approach reproduction, root-cause analysis, and verification.

Scope
Order persistence & UI feedback
Risk
Misleading success confirmation
Focus
Async ordering & outcome assertions
Investigate this case ↗
01

Reproduce & capture

Check persisted state when the notification appears. Capture notification and persistence events on a shared timeline.

02

Distinguish cause from symptom

The demo confirms that the save is started without awaiting completion. The notification alone cannot establish persistence.

03

Correct & verify

Await persistence before reporting success. Rerun the same check against the corrected event sequence.

04

State the limits

A passing simulation verifies this ordering scenario. A production release also needs failed-save handling, integration checks, and relevant regression coverage.

Read the stakeholder update +

The order confirmation appeared before persistence completed in the reproduced scenario. The updated sequence waits for completion before showing success. The same check now passes in the browser model. Production readiness would still require integration validation, failed-save coverage, and regression testing.
